numbering.collection: Alphabetical position across the 25 wt-pm repositories (01-25). This is the number printed on each repository's page and used in the repository names you already know.
numbering.adapter: Task-based platform adapter id (m01-m25). This is the id the ModelRegistry, the wt-pm CLI and the fusion engine use.

edgeai.name: Edge AI
edgeai.note: Models that run at or near the turbine: compressing telemetry for backhaul, extracting features on low-power hardware, and tripping safety relays without waiting for the cloud.

anomaly.name: SCADA Anomaly Detection
anomaly.note: Seven detectors over the shared 12-channel, 10-minute SCADA contract. Different inductive biases - sequences, reconstruction, boundaries, forests, attention - one output record, so downstream layers never care which one fired.

fault.name: Component Fault Classification
fault.note: Turning 'something is wrong' into 'this component, this failure mode'. Consumes anomaly records and edge features; produces the labels that prognostics and XAI operate on.

rul.name: RUL Prognostics
rul.note: Remaining-useful-life estimation: discrete degradation states, spatiotemporal wear tracking, learned feature hierarchies, probabilistic filtering - anchored by a deliberately simple MLP baseline.

physics.name: Physics-Informed & Explainable
physics.note: The layer that keeps the learning honest: physics surrogates supply residuals and constraints, and SHAP/LIME turn alerts into root-cause explanations.

models.title: 1D-CNN Bearing Vibration
models.summary: A three-block 1D convolutional network that classifies gearbox bearing condition directly from a raw vibration window, with no hand-built spectral features. It is the highest-resolution view of the drivetrain in the collection: the only model that would consume a real high-frequency DAQ stream unchanged if one were wired to the simulator.
entry_points: python model.py - prints the layer summary

architecture.detail: 3 x (Conv1D kernel 3 + ReLU -> MaxPooling1D 2), 32 -> 64 -> 128 filters; learns its own band-pass banks instead of an FFT
Flatten -> Dense(128) + ReLU -> Dropout(0.5) -> Dense(num_classes) + softmax
Adam, categorical_crossentropy; 2,096,068 parameters for (1024, 1) input and 4 classes

io.input: 1024-sample vibration waveform windows - surrogates synthesised from bearing_vib_rms_mm_s and flagged vibration_is_surrogate=True
io.output: prediction + probability over healthy / bearing_wear / imbalance / other

advanced.detail: Three kernel-3 convolutions separated by max-pool 2 give a receptive field of 1 + 2 + 4 + ... samples of context per output activation. Widening the kernel or adding a dilation is the only way to see a full shaft revolution without a deeper stack - the reason the upstream model stops at 1024 samples.

Classical bearing diagnostics hand you envelope spectra and defect frequencies (BPFO/BPFI). A 1D-CNN learns its own filter bank end to end, which is why it transfers across machines - and why it needs thousands of labelled windows to beat the handcrafted baseline at all.

The platform has 10-minute RMS SCADA, not 20 kHz DAQ. Waveforms are synthesised and carry vibration_is_surrogate=True, so every metric this model reports is a property of the pipeline, not of a real bearing. Swapping in a real DAQ path changes only the adapter's input view, never the network.

layers.detail: Drivetrain fault voter in the classification fusion - a softmax vote, not a score threshold
Feeds the diagnose tool: turns an anomaly into a named failure mode and a subsystem (WHERE)
Its alert is explained by m21 SHAP over the tabular features plus a contrastive healthy-band comparison
Trains only on windows fully inside train_mask - no window is allowed to straddle a held-out row

limits: Surrogate waveforms, not field DAQ - vibration_is_surrogate=True on every record
Metrics are held-out simulator records (fidelity rung 1), not certified asset performance

models.title: AeroZip Autoencoder Compressor
models.summary: An 8:1 bottleneck autoencoder that squeezes a 64-column telemetry table into an 8-dimensional latent vector for low-bandwidth cellular or satellite backhaul. The same latent doubles as a feature stream for the rest of the collection, so compression is not a separate pipeline stage - it is the first one.

architecture.detail: Linear(input_dim, 32) -> ReLU -> Linear(32, latent_dim)
Linear(latent_dim, 32) -> ReLU -> Linear(32, input_dim)
Returns both tensors: the latent is the product, the reconstruction is the loss signal
4,744 parameters at 64 -> 8; 2,794 when the platform instantiates it on its 38-column feature table with latent_dim=4

advanced.detail: 8:1 is a count of dimensions, not of bytes actually sent. A defensible bandwidth claim needs entropy-coded latent bitrates measured on real backhaul traces - the model reports compression_ratio() and nothing more.

advanced.concept: Reconstruction error as a free detector
advanced.detail: An autoencoder trained on healthy telemetry misfits when the plant changes. The same forward pass therefore yields two products: a latent for backhaul and a scalar residual that behaves like an unsupervised anomaly score.
The bottleneck is reused as the input view for the tabular voters (m10, m11) and the SSL encoder, so a cheap linear layer at the edge can produce features the cloud classifiers already understand.

layers.detail: Supplies features rather than votes; the feature_extraction stage feeds m08 / m09 / m10 / m11
Deploys to edge CPU and GPU; it is the only compressor in the collection, so it is the assumed front end for constrained links
Rising reconstruction error on live data is the earliest drift signal in the pipeline - evaluated by evaluation.drift_report
Its latent feeds the anomaly and diagnose tools indirectly through the downstream voters

limits: Backhaul byte savings are not measured - only the dimensional ratio is
Latent quality is validated on simulator statistics, not on a real link budget

models.title: Contrastive SSL Vibration
models.status: partial (SimCLR encoder; platform adapter supplies full NT-Xent loss)
models.summary: A SimCLR-style encoder that learns vibration representations without any labels by pulling two augmented views of the same window together and pushing every other window apart. In a plant where failures are rare and unlabelled data is abundant, this is the model that manufactures the labels nobody has.
entry_points: Platform adapter supplies the complete NT-Xent loss the repository omits

architecture.detail: Shared-weight convolutional / MLP trunk producing one embedding per view
Small MLP mapping embeddings onto the unit sphere where the contrastive loss is computed
NT-Xent over 2N augmented views with a temperature parameter; upstream ships a partial implementation, completed by the adapter

io.input: unlabelled vibration windows (two augmented views per sample)

advanced.detail: The loss is a softmax over cosine similarities scaled by 1/temperature. Temperature controls how hard the model punishes near-miss negatives - too low and training collapses, too high and the representation stops discriminating.

You are not learning 'normal vibration'; you are learning whatever the augmentation pipeline refuses to change - jitter, amplitude scaling, time shifts. Choose augmentations that are physically irrelevant and the embedding becomes a fault fingerprint.

The upstream repository defines the encoder but not the full loss. The platform adapter implements it, which is why this model is marked partial rather than complete: the numbers describe the platform's training loop, not the upstream repo's.

layers.detail: Feature extractor: no vote of its own, improves everyone else's features
Pretraining uses unlabelled windows only; the linear probe is evaluated on held-out rows so no label leaks backwards
Embeddings power the contrastive healthy-band z-score used by the XAI bundle
Embedding-space drift is the most sensitive early warning the platform has, because it needs no labels

models.hermes: no direct tool - improves anomaly / diagnose evidence
limits: Upstream loss incomplete; performance is attributable to the platform's completed NT-Xent
No downstream fine-tuning is shipped for every classifier - some consume features as-is

models.title: ConvLSTM Wear Prognostics
models.status: partial (repo expects 64x64 wear maps; platform builds channel-recurrence images)
models.summary: A ConvLSTM2D stack that carries a two-dimensional wear field forward in time, keeping spatial structure that a plain LSTM would flatten away. It is the collection's spatiotemporal degradation tracker - and its bluntest example of how a research assumption meets a data reality.
entry_points: Platform adapter builds recurrence images from the 12-channel window

architecture.detail: Upstream expects (10, 64, 64, 1) wear maps - a sequence of ten 64x64 frames
ConvLSTM2D cells replace the dense gates of an LSTM with convolutions, so hidden state keeps a spatial extent
Regression onto remaining useful life

io.input: windows -> 16x16 channel-recurrence images (the platform's substitute for unavailable wear maps)

advanced.detail: Every gate in a ConvLSTM is itself a convolution, so the cell learns where to remember as well as when. That is what makes it suitable for a degradation field, and what makes it 10-100x more expensive than a dense recurrent layer.

No data source in the collection produces wear maps. Rather than silently fabricating them, the adapter builds 16x16 channel-recurrence images and the model is marked partial. The honest statement is: the recurrence works, the upstream spatial claim is untested.

A point estimate of remaining life is almost useless for planning without an interval. This adapter returns rul_hours only; the probabilistic statement comes from m16, which fuses these observations into a posterior.

layers.detail: One of the RUL observations consumed by the m16 particle filter
Scored with rul_metrics (MAE / RMSE / asymmetric penalty), not with classification metrics
Feeds the rul tool alongside m15 states and m17 baseline
Falls back to m17-mlp-rul when TensorFlow is unavailable - the platform never fails a question because a heavy model is missing

limits: Partial: upstream 64x64 wear-map contract is not satisfiable with available data
15 s typical latency - cloud only, never in the safety path

models.title: DBN Feature Extraction
models.status: integrated (platform supplies its own CD-1 loop; the repo ships one too)
models.summary: A stack of Restricted Boltzmann Machines trained greedily layer by layer, then read out as a feature hierarchy for wear tracking. It is the classic pre-deep-learning answer to 'we do not have enough labels', and it still earns its place because its features are interpretable as successive energy minima.
entry_points: Contrastive-divergence (CD-1) training loop - present in the repo and re-implemented by the adapter

architecture.detail: Visible-hidden bipartite energy model; each unit is a Bernoulli or Gaussian variable
CD-1 Gibbs sampling per layer - one negative-phase step is enough for a usable gradient estimate
Upper-layer activations become features for the RUL regressors

io.input: feature vectors (no labels required for pretraining)

advanced.detail: An RBM defines an energy for every visible-hidden configuration; learning lowers the energy of data and raises it elsewhere. The gradient needs the model's own expectation, which is intractable - that is the whole reason for contrastive divergence.

advanced.concept: Why one Gibbs step is enough
advanced.detail: CD-1 is biased but cheap: it does not follow the true gradient, yet it reliably moves parameters in a useful direction. The bias is why DBNs were displaced by backpropagation-based autoencoders, and why the repo's CD-1 loop matters for reproducing the numbers.

Each layer's activations are a legitimate feature set, so you can stop early for a cheaper model. The platform treats the DBN as a feature provider, which is how it can serve an RUL regressor without retraining anything downstream.

layers.detail: Feature extractor feeding the m17 RUL regressor and the tabular voters
Pretraining masks exclude held-out rows entirely, so unsupervised structure cannot leak test labels
Judged by downstream RUL error, not by reconstruction loss - a lower CD-1 objective is not automatically a better feature
Layer activations are inspectable, which makes the DBN the most auditable feature extractor in the collection

limits: No GPU path; 3 s latency keeps it on the server
CD-1 bias is accepted, not corrected - numbers are reproducible, not optimal

models.title: Deep SVDD Boundary
models.status: integrated (6-layer bias-free encoder; platform supplies its own training loop)
models.summary: A neural network trained to map healthy telemetry into a tight hypersphere, so that abnormality is literally distance from the centre. Unlike reconstruction models it never learns what a fault looks like - it only learns the shape of normal, which is exactly the assumption a wind farm can support.

architecture.detail: 6 layers, no bias terms - a deliberate constraint that stops the network from shrinking the sphere by shifting it
init_center() fixes c as the mean of the encoder outputs on healthy data, then freezes it
svdd_loss minimises squared distance to c plus L2 weight decay; the weight decay is what prevents hypersphere collapse
Robust-calibrated distance to the centre becomes anomaly_score

io.output: anomaly_score - robust-calibrated distance to the hypersphere centre

advanced.detail: If you let a network map everything to one point, the loss goes to zero and the model dies. The classical fixes are the bias-free encoder plus weight decay - both are present here, and both are the reason this is a usable detector rather than a degenerate one.

Deep SVDD trains on healthy data only. That is its strength (no fault labels needed) and its blind spot: it cannot distinguish a new normal operating regime from a fault unless the encoders around it disagree.

init_center() from a healthy sample biases the whole solution. Averaging over a representative healthy window - and refusing to move c afterwards - is what makes the anomaly score comparable across turbines.

layers.detail: One of seven anomaly voters; its score is combined by the confidence-weighted fusion rule
anomaly tool - contributes a boundary verdict rather than a forecasting one
Falls back to m14-isolation-forest when torch is absent
A slow drift of the encoder's mean distance is a hygiene signal that the healthy reference has gone stale

limits: Requires a trustworthy healthy window to fix the centre
Distance is not a probability - calibration is done by robust scaling, not by likelihood

models.title: Digital Twin Surrogate
models.summary: A neural surrogate that stands in for a finite-element model, returning stress, deflection and fatigue proxies in about a millisecond instead of hours. Its real product is the residual: what the physics says should be happening versus what the SCADA actually reports.
entry_points: Platform adapter trains it against simulator physics proxies

architecture.detail: Operating-condition channels - wind speed, rotor speed, pitch, power
Feed-forward MLP replacing the FEA solve
Thrust ~ rho * v^2, bending and fatigue proxies derived from the simulator's own physics

advanced.detail: FEA of a blade or tower is accurate and unusable online. A surrogate trained offline reproduces the input-output map in milliseconds, which is what makes physics available inside a 10-minute SCADA loop.

The model never claims to find faults. It predicts what physics implies, and the mismatch between prediction and measurement is handed to the anomaly voters - physics constrains the learning rather than replacing it.

A surrogate is only valid inside its training envelope. Outside rated wind or in a new control strategy its residuals grow for reasons that have nothing to do with damage, which is why residuals are clustered with, never substituted for, the statistical detectors.

layers.detail: what_if tool - the only model that answers 'what if we pitch two degrees differently'
Physics residuals feed the anomaly ensemble as an extra evidence stream (support task, no vote weight of its own)
Gives the explanation layer a physical counterfactual to compare against the statistical one
Scored on regression error against the physics proxy targets, not on fault detection

limits: Targets are simulator physics proxies, not measured loads
No valid extrapolation outside the training envelope

models.title: GNN Turbine Cascade
models.summary: A graph neural network that lifts per-turbine evidence onto a wake-coupled farm graph, so a fault upstream can raise the risk estimate downstream. It is the only model in the collection whose unit of analysis is the fleet rather than the machine.
entry_points: Fallback linear network when torch-geometric is absent

architecture.detail: Nodes are turbines; edges encode wake coupling supplied in meta['fleet']
Each node aggregates neighbour states, so evidence propagates along the wake direction
Per-node cascade risk class

io.output: prediction - cascade risk class per turbine
deps: torch-geometric (optional: the repo ships a fallback)

advanced.detail: Each layer replaces a node's features with a learned aggregation of its neighbours'. Stacking k layers gives every turbine a receptive field of k wake hops, which is how a local fault becomes a farm-level statement.

Upstream training uses self-loop synthetic vibration-risk labels. The fixed weights are applied to the supplied fleet graph, so this model demonstrates the mechanism rather than a validated wake-physics result.
Downstream, cascade risk conditions RUL updates in m16 - a turbine behind a poorly performing neighbour gets a wider uncertainty interval even when its own signals look clean.

layers.detail: Fleet-risk context attached to the diagnosis, not blended into the per-turbine score
Context for diagnose and rul - explains why a clean-looking turbine still carries risk
Cascade risk conditions the m16 particle filter's observation noise
Graph-native metrics; per-node accuracy alone would hide propagation errors

limits: Trained against self-loop synthetic supervision, not validated wake physics
Wake graph comes from the simulator's layout, not from a met-mast campaign

models.title: GRU SCADA Telemetry
models.summary: A one-step-ahead GRU forecaster over the 12 SCADA channels whose prediction error is the anomaly score. It is the cheapest sequence detector in the collection and the one that runs on an edge CPU, which makes it the default continuous monitor.
entry_points: python model.py - defines the class; loads no data and trains nothing

architecture.detail: nn.GRU(input_size, hidden_size, num_layers, batch_first=True)
nn.Linear(hidden_size, input_size) - predicts the next step of every channel from the final hidden state
Standardised one-step forecast error; no reconstruction decoder is needed

io.input: sequence windows over the canonical 12 SCADA channels

advanced.detail: The GRU's reset gate decides how much past state to forget and the update gate how much new candidate state to admit. Two gates instead of the LSTM's three is why this model fits an edge CPU's latency budget at 2 s per window.

A one-step forecast error is a residual, not a horizon forecast: it says 'this moment did not follow from the last few', which is the right question for detection and the wrong one for planning. Horizon forecasting is m06's job.

Raw squared error scales with the channel's own range, so a gusty day looks like a fault. The adapter standardises error before it becomes a score - the reason the fusion layer can compare this vote with SVDD and VAE distances at all.

layers.detail: Anomaly voter; confidence-weighted fusion down-weights it when the wrapped uncertainty is high
anomaly tool - the GRU's residual is one of the votes the agent observes
Runs on edge CPU, so it is the detector that survives when the backhaul drops
Falls back to m14-isolation-forest when torch is unavailable

limits: Architecture only upstream - the platform supplies the training loop (short fits on simulator windows)
Metrics are held-out simulator records (fidelity rung 1), not certified asset performance

models.title: HMM Degradation States
models.summary: A Gaussian hidden Markov model that infers the unobservable degradation stage behind a continuous health indicator, and emits a probability over discrete states rather than a number. It answers HOW SEVERE in a form a maintenance planner can act on.
entry_points: Platform adapter re-orders states by mean health indicator

architecture.detail: Discrete degradation stages with Gaussian emission per state
Baum-Welch for parameters, forward-backward for the posterior state distribution given the whole history
States are permuted so that index == severity, which makes the label stable across refits and seeds

advanced.detail: A hidden state is not a cluster. The posterior is computed over the whole sequence with forward-backward, so yesterday's evidence changes today's state estimate - the smoothing a static classifier cannot do.

HMM state indices are arbitrary; refitting with a different seed can swap state 1 and state 3. Sorting states by mean health indicator is what turns a research object into a monotone severity scale the platform can report.

The state transition rate is a degradation rate, and m16 consumes it as the process model for a probabilistic RUL posterior. Discrete states plus a continuous filter is the collection's bridge from 'how bad' to 'how long'.

layers.detail: Supplies the degradation_state field that classification and RUL layers attach to
Where the agent's SEVERE answer comes from - a posterior over states, not a threshold
State transitions seed the m16 particle filter
Scored on state-posterior calibration and transition timing, not on point accuracy alone

limits: Standard HMM assumptions: Gaussian emissions, first-order Markov transitions
Requires a health indicator that is already monotone in damage

models.title: Informer Long Sequence
models.summary: A long-horizon transformer forecaster for farm power, built on sparse attention that scales linearly instead of quadratically in sequence length. Its forecast residual is an anomaly signal, and its horizon is what makes day-ahead planning possible at all.
entry_points: ProbSparse attention block - self-declared placeholder upstream

architecture.detail: ProbSparse self-attention plus a distilling step that halves sequence length per layer
Generative-style decoder producing the whole forecast horizon in one forward pass
Multi-step power forecast; residual against actuals becomes the anomaly score

advanced.detail: Only the queries with the most 'active' attention distributions are evaluated, reducing cost from O(L^2) to O(L log L). That is the entire reason a long-horizon transformer is deployable on 10-minute SCADA at all.
Each encoder layer halves the sequence, so depth buys global context instead of memory. The trade is resolution: fine structure must be captured early or it is gone.

Upstream ships a placeholder attention implementation. The adapter runs the real graph but the attention is not the published ProbSparse kernel, so the forecast error is honest but the architecture claim is not. Marking it partial is the point.

layers.detail: Forecast-residual anomaly voter and the long-horizon source for power-curve tracking
anomaly tool plus planning context for what_if
Falls back to m03-tcn-power-curve when torch is unavailable
Scored on both forecast error and residual-based detection - a good forecaster can be a poor detector

limits: Partial: attention is a placeholder, so results are not the published Informer
8 s latency - cloud only

models.title: Isolation Forest Telemetry
models.summary: An ensemble of random trees that isolates outliers by how few splits they need to become alone. It is the cheapest detector in the collection, needs no training labels, and is the fallback every heavy model degrades to - which makes it the reason the platform still answers when a dependency is missing.

architecture.detail: Random subsamples of rows; each tree splits on a random feature at a random threshold
Anomaly score is a monotone function of average isolation depth - short paths are outliers
Near-linear in rows, sub-second on a SCADA window

advanced.detail: Most detectors model normal and measure deviation. Isolation Forest measures how easy a point is to separate - a genuinely different inductive bias, and the reason it stays useful when the 'normal' distribution is multimodal.

advanced.concept: Contamination is a decision, not a parameter
advanced.detail: The model outputs a score; turning it into an alert needs an assumed contamination rate. The platform keeps that choice at the fusion/alert layer so the alert rate is set once for the fleet, not per model.

advanced.concept: The fallback that must not fail
advanced.detail: m03, m04, m05, m13 and m22 all declare m14 as their fallback. That makes it the platform's availability guarantee: no missing torch install can leave a turbine unmonitored.

layers.detail: Anomaly voter and universal fallback - its weight is learned in research mode via evaluation.select_weights
Sub-second and sklearn-only, so it runs wherever Python runs
anomaly tool; also the evidence the agent sees when a heavy detector is unavailable
Its score is thresholded through the AlertManager's hysteresis and cooldown, not per call

limits: Scores are not probabilities and drift with the contamination assumption
Blind to temporal structure - it sees a feature vector, not a sequence

models.title: LSTM SCADA Anomaly (reference contract hub)
models.status: integrated - reference implementation and platform host
models.summary: The original LSTM/GRU autoencoder over the 12-channel SCADA schema - and the repository that defines the contract every other model in the collection adopts: WTDataSchema, the record format, the physics simulator, the drift report, the evaluation protocol, the HTTP API and the unified platform itself.
entry_points: wtpm - the model 13 CLI (demo, serve, train, evaluate)
wt-pm - the 25-model platform CLI shipped from platform/

architecture.detail: LSTM or GRU sequence autoencoder with a configurable latent bottleneck; reconstruction error per timestamp
12 canonical channels over 10-minute samples, validated by WTDataSchema - temperature, vibration RMS, power, wind, rotor speed, currents, grid frequency
Threshold chosen on a healthy holdout, with the same protocol the other 24 models are scored under
Rolling distribution comparison between training and live features, reported as a first-class object rather than a footnote

advanced.detail: This repository is model 13 of 25 alphabetically and adapter m05-lstm-scada-anomaly by task. Both are printed on every page in the collection so a reader can cross-reference the ecosystem graph and the platform registry without guessing.

Nothing here is patched into the siblings. Each is wrapped by an adapter that imports its original model.py. The contract is the interface: timestamp, turbine_id and model_id are required; the rest of the record is optional so a model can fill in as little as it honestly knows.

The protocol module rejects any training window that touches an excluded row and holds past-only state before the first observation. Ten minutes of context is not allowed to smuggle future evidence into a held-out evaluation.
The detector reports an interval alongside its score, which is what lets the fusion engine use inverse-variance weighting instead of treating every vote as equally confident.

layers.detail: Owns WTDataSchema, the record format, the simulator and the fidelity ladder the other 24 pages cite
Anomaly voter and the reference implementation of thresholding and attribution
anomaly and finish; the simulator it ships is what the agent's observations are grounded in
Defines the held-out protocol, the drift report and the rung-1 fidelity ceiling
FastAPI/HTTP service with /health, /ready and the analysis endpoint the Render deployment runs

limits: Simulator is synthetic; rung-1 fidelity only
The platform's numbers describe the wrapped pipelines, not field-validated turbine control

models.title: MLP RUL Regression
models.summary: A plain multi-layer perceptron regressing remaining useful life from accumulated operating hours and features. It exists to be beaten: every fancier prognostic in the collection has to show it adds value over this baseline.
entry_points: sklearn MLPRegressor under the platform adapter

architecture.detail: Feature table, optionally including accumulated operating hours
One or two hidden layers with ReLU - deliberately small
RUL proxy: time to fault onset in the simulator

advanced.detail: A prognostic result without a baseline is unfalsifiable. Because this model is in the same registry, same protocol and same held-out split, every claim from ConvLSTM, HMM or the particle filter can be stated as an improvement over a number that is visible.

RUL is not measured in the simulator; time-to-fault-onset is. The target is a proxy, and the fidelity ladder says so - which is why 'hours' on these pages are comparable across models and not to a real asset.

On short records with strong monotone covariates, a small MLP is hard to beat and impossible to beat on cost. Its weakness is exactly that it cannot represent sequence state - the gap the recurrent and filtering models are supposed to close.

layers.detail: RUL observation for m16; the reference point in RUL comparisons
m02-convlstm-wear falls back here when TensorFlow is missing
rul tool - reports the point estimate the probabilistic models must improve on
Scored with rul_metrics alongside every other prognostic

limits: Proxy RUL target, not measured remaining life
No uncertainty interval - a point estimate only

models.title: Particle Filter RUL
models.summary: A sequential Monte Carlo filter that fuses the RUL observations of its sibling models into a full posterior distribution over remaining life. It is the only prognostic in the collection that reports uncertainty as a distribution rather than a number, and it is pure NumPy - no deep-learning stack required.
entry_points: Platform adapter wraps it and feeds sibling RUL estimates as observations

architecture.detail: Hidden degradation state and its rate of change
Weighted samples propagated through the state-transition model
Likelihood from m17 / m02 RUL estimates; resampling when effective sample size collapses
Posterior mean and quantiles of remaining useful life

io.input: RUL observations from m17 / m02 + degradation rate from m15

advanced.detail: The posterior is represented by particles instead of a closed form, which is what allows a non-linear degradation model without an extended or unscented Kalman approximation. Cost is linear in particle count and constant in time.

After a few updates almost all weight concentrates on a handful of particles. The effective-sample-size trigger and systematic resampling are the difference between a working filter and one that silently reports the same number forever.

This model does not train a network. It treats m17 and m02 outputs as noisy observations and m15's transition rate as the process model - a genuinely composable prognostic, and the clearest example of the collection behaving like a platform.
A maintenance window needs a quantile, not a mean. The filter returns a distribution, so the planner can quote 'P(failure within 30 days)' rather than a single hour count.

layers.detail: Consumes other models' outputs rather than raw sensors - the fusion layer's downstream client
rul tool: supplies the interval that turns a maintenance recommendation into a decision
One of only two models (with m18 PG-BNN) that emits a calibrated uncertainty field
Its posterior feeds the CostRiskOptimizer's continue / derate / inspect / trip expected-cost comparison

limits: Result quality is bounded by the observation models it consumes
State-transition model is a simulator-derived degradation law, not wear physics

models.title: PG-BNN Physics-Guided Bayesian
models.status: integrated (BNN assembled from the repo's blocks)
models.summary: A Bayesian neural network that predicts power under a P = tau * omega physics constraint and reports epistemic uncertainty by Monte Carlo sampling its own weights. It is the collection's answer to 'how much should we trust this model on conditions it has never seen'.
entry_points: Platform adapter assembles the full physics-guided model

architecture.detail: BayesianLinear layers sampling weights per forward pass - variational inference over parameters
Loss includes a P = tau * omega consistency term between predicted power, torque and rotor speed
Mean prediction plus MC-sampled variance; power residual feeds the anomaly score

advanced.detail: A point prediction that is wrong is useless; a prediction with a wide interval because the operating point is novel is actionable. MC sampling over the weight posterior captures the epistemic part - uncertainty that shrinks as data arrives.

P = tau * omega is not enforced as a hard layer but as a penalty term. That keeps the model differentiable and lets the data override the constraint where the constraint is wrong - a trade the pages state openly.

When the physics-guided branch is confident and the statistical detectors are not, the disagreement itself is evidence. Fusion treats m18 as an anomaly voter and an uncertainty source rather than an oracle.

layers.detail: Second of the two uncertainty emitters; enables inverse-variance weighting in the fusion engine
Receives constraints from the m19 digital twin and returns physics-consistent residuals
anomaly tool with an explicit confidence attached to every observation
Physics-guided uncertainty propagates into m16's RUL posterior

limits: Variational approximation, not exact posterior inference
Physics term is a soft penalty against the simulator's own physics

models.title: Quantized MobileNet Edge
models.status: integrated (INT8 recipe applied to the platform's edge net)
models.summary: An INT8 post-training quantization recipe that turns a float model into a TFLite artifact small enough for constrained hardware, with a measured byte size reported on every inference record. On this collection it is applied to a compact edge network, because no image data exists for full MobileNet.
entry_points: TFLite converter + quantization recipe in model.py
Platform adapter applies it to the platform edge net and reports size_bytes

architecture.detail: A calibration set determines the affine scale and zero point for every activation
Post-training INT8 conversion - weights and activations to 8-bit integers
TFLite flatbuffer; size_bytes is emitted on the model output so the edge budget is visible

io.input: features (+ fault labels for the research fit only)

advanced.detail: INT8 stores x approximately as scale * (q - zero_point). The whole game is choosing the calibration ranges so that values near zero keep resolution and rare spikes do not dominate the scale.

Post-training quantization typically costs one to three points of accuracy and roughly 4x in model size. The platform makes that trade visible by reporting size_bytes far more prominently than a percentage it cannot independently verify on target hardware.

Full MobileNet expects 224x224 images. This collection has none, so the recipe is applied to the platform's small edge net. The page says so instead of quoting a MobileNet benchmark that could not have been reproduced here.

layers.detail: Produces the deployable artifact family - the same pipeline that exports the m25 relay's C++ header
Its predictions enter the classification vote as a low-power voter
Accuracy and size are both tracked; a smaller model that lost its class separation is not a win
diagnose tool when the deployment target is edge CPU or MCU-adjacent

limits: Recipe applied to a compact edge net, not to full 224x224 MobileNet
Target-hardware latency is not measured - only the cloud build path is end-to-end verified

models.title: Random Forest Telemetry
models.summary: A bagged tree ensemble that classifies sensor-diagnostic fault classes and hands its feature importances to the explanation layer. It is the collection's most transparent classifier: every vote can be traced back to impure splits over named channels.

architecture.detail: Each tree sees a bootstrap resample; averaging decorrelates their errors
A random feature subset per split keeps trees diverse
Gini importance per feature, exported as model evidence for the XAI bundle

advanced.detail: Random Forest averages deep, low-bias trees; boosting adds shallow, high-bias ones. Averaging is harder to overfit and much easier to explain, which is why both this and m11 exist in the collection rather than one of them.

Impurity importance favours high-cardinality and high-variance columns. The platform treats it as a ranked hint and lets m21 SHAP produce the additive, signed attribution - importance ranks, SHAP explains.
Averaged leaf votes are not calibrated probabilities. Evaluation computes expected calibration error so an over-confident forest is visible before it reaches an operator.

layers.detail: Fault-class voter; the coverage-aware probability fusion ignores classes a model abstains on
Supplies feature_importances to the XAI evidence bundle alongside m21 SHAP values
diagnose tool - one of the honest votes behind WHERE
600 ms and sklearn-only: it is one of the classifiers distilled toward the m25 safety path

limits: Gini importances are not causal attributions
Trained on simulator fault classes - the label set is the simulator's, not a plant's

models.title: SNN Event Vibration
models.summary: A spiking neural network that consumes vibration as asynchronous threshold-crossing events rather than as a sampled waveform, and reads out class evidence from spike rates. It is the collection's ultra-low-power path: spikes cost energy only when they fire.
entry_points: Delta / threshold event encoder supplied by the adapter

architecture.detail: A sample is transmitted only when it moves more than delta from the last transmitted value
Leaky integrate-and-fire cells accumulate input until a membrane threshold, then emit a spike and reset
Differentiable membrane potential logits converted to class evidence via spike rates

advanced.detail: Delta encoding throws away everything that did not change. On a wind turbine that is most samples, which is the real energy argument - not the network, the fact that steady state costs nothing to transmit.

A spike is a step function with zero derivative almost everywhere, so backpropagation needs a surrogate gradient. That approximation, not the spiking itself, is where the accuracy comes from - and where it is most fragile.

Reading the differentiable membrane potential rather than raw spike counts gives a smooth, fusable score. The adapter uses it exactly like any other softmax voter, so the fusion engine needs no special case for neuromorphic hardware.

layers.detail: Drivetrain classification voter, interchangeable with m01's vote in the ensemble
Listed for edge CPU and GPU - the intended destination of event-driven inference
diagnose tool; its spike-rate evidence appears in the agent's observation list
Falls back to m01-1dcnn-bearing when snnTorch is unavailable

limits: Events are synthesised from surrogate waveforms, not from a neuromorphic sensor
Energy claims are architectural - no joule measurements on spiking hardware

models.title: SVM-RBF Generator Stator
models.summary: A support-vector machine with an RBF kernel specialised on the electrical channels, separating generator stator and rotor insulation faults from normal converter behaviour. It is the one classifier whose feature space is deliberately narrow: it looks at volts and amps, not at vibration.

architecture.detail: Electrical channels only - currents, voltages, grid frequency, power factor proxies
RBF kernel maps features into an implicit higher-dimensional space where a maximum-margin hyperplane separates the classes
Platt scaling turns decision-function distances into usable probabilities

io.input: electrical features (+ labels in research mode)

advanced.detail: An RBF SVM never materialises the higher-dimensional space; it only needs pairwise similarities. That is what lets it draw a curved boundary in a 5-column electrical space without the parameter count of a multilayer network.
Stator insulation faults are rare, so class-weighted margins matter more than raw accuracy. A model that predicts 'healthy' for everything can look excellent on an unbalanced split.

advanced.concept: Platt scaling is not calibration by default
advanced.detail: The probability outputs come from a fitted sigmoid on decision distances and can be mis-calibrated on shifted data. Expected calibration error is computed at evaluation time alongside ROC-AUC for exactly this reason.

layers.detail: Electrical specialist vote - it usually disagrees with the vibration models, which is the point of a diverse ensemble
diagnose tool; narrows WHERE to generator/converter instead of the drivetrain
Falls back to m11-xgboost-tabular on non-electrical evidence
Scored with ROC-AUC, PR-AUC and calibration on a held-out split

limits: Binary electrical-fault separation, not a full fault taxonomy
Sensitive to the scaling of electrical features - no raw-amplitude inference

models.title: TCN Power Curve
models.summary: A causal temporal convolutional network that tracks the aerodynamic power curve and flags residual drift away from it. It is the collection's fastest way to answer the oldest question in wind O&M: is this turbine producing what its own history says it should at this wind speed?
entry_points: Platform adapter trains it against the power channel

architecture.detail: Kernel size k over L layers with exponentially growing dilation; the receptive field grows as (k-1) * 2^L
Each block adds its input back, which keeps deep stacks trainable
Power forecast for the next step; residual against measured power is the anomaly score

advanced.detail: Two conv layers with kernel 3 see 5 samples; with dilation 1, 2, 4 the same two layers see 15. Causal TCNs buy long memory with convolution parallelism instead of recurrence's sequential dependency.

The bin-mean power curve is the industry's simplest performance model. Modelling the residual lets the network absorb wind-speed binning, air density and control mode explicitly rather than forcing the reader to attribute them.

A residual can mean blade erosion, a dirty filter, icing or a curtailment instruction. The anomaly record is honest about being a performance signal; classification and XAI decide whether it is a fault.

layers.detail: Anomaly voter and the fallback target for m06's long-horizon forecasts
anomaly tool - power-curve residual is the first thing the agent checks on an underperformance question
Power-curve degradation is an input feature for the RUL regressors
Receives falls back from m06 and falls back to m04 itself

limits: A performance residual is not a fault label - curtailment and icing look identical statistically
Causal convolutions trade receptive field for latency headroom on the edge

models.title: TinyML ESP32 Safety Relay
models.summary: A depth-5 decision tree compiled to C++ and dropped onto an ESP32, plus a mirrored in-loop gate that trips on the same hard limits before SCADA is ever written. It is the only model allowed to say STOP, and the only one whose failure mode is physical.
entry_points: micromlgen export producing model.h for the ESP32 firmware

architecture.detail: Depth-5 decision tree over bearing_vib_rms_mm_s, gearbox_oil_temp_c, rotor_speed_rpm and power_kw
model.h C++ header generated by micromlgen, compiled into bare-metal firmware
The SafetyManager re-evaluates the same limits in-process, so the platform's answer and the rail's answer cannot diverge silently

io.input: safety channels - bearing_vib_rms_mm_s, gearbox_oil_temp_c, rotor_speed_rpm, power_kw

advanced.detail: On an ESP32 the constraint is not accuracy, it is deterministic 50 ms latency with no allocator and no floating-point surprise. A depth-5 tree is a handful of comparisons - auditable, certifiable and impossible to make non-deterministic.

micromlgen emits C++, so the model stops being an artifact and becomes firmware. That is a different trust boundary from every other model here: no dependency can go missing at runtime because there is no runtime.

The C++ tree and the in-loop SafetyManager evaluate the same limits. Divergence between them is a detectable fault of its own - the platform reports the mirrored decision so an operator can see whether the rail and the cloud agree.
m25 never enters the fusion weighting. It is excluded from the ensemble by construction: an average of opinions is not a protection function.

layers.detail: Hard limits and trips; the only model permitted to veto, and excluded from fusion weighting
safety tool - the SAFE answer in the agent's summary
The only model declaring the MCU deployment target; the router categorically refuses to send any other model there
Its decisions are recorded in the DecisionAuditLog alongside the analysis that produced them

limits: Fixed depth-5 structure - it cannot express a fault it was not shaped for
Limits are configuration, not derived from a certified safety case; this is a research demo, not a SIL-rated protection system

models.title: VAE Reconstruction Loss
models.summary: A variational autoencoder whose reconstruction error flags rare non-linear sensor anomalies, with a latent distribution that makes the score a likelihood rather than a distance. It is the collection's probabilistic reconstruction model.
entry_points: Platform adapter trains and scores with the repository's own loss

architecture.detail: Maps a window to a Gaussian posterior (mean, log-variance) over the latent code
z = mu + sigma * epsilon, which keeps the sampling path differentiable
Reconstruction term minus KL divergence to the prior - the repo's vae_loss
Per-timestamp reconstruction error, standardised against the healthy band

advanced.detail: The loss balances two goals that fight: reconstruct faithfully and stay close to the prior. Weighting the KL term harder (a beta-VAE) gives a smoother, more regular latent space and blurrier reconstructions - a real dial on how sensitive the detector is.

If the decoder is expressive enough, it ignores the latent code entirely and the KL term goes to zero. Recognising collapse matters operationally: the model still produces numbers, they are just no longer a latent-variable statement.
Because the latent is a distribution, repeated sampling yields a spread on the reconstruction error. That is what the adapter reports as uncertainty, and what lets fusion discount a shaky VAE vote.

layers.detail: Anomaly voter with an attached uncertainty - eligible for inverse-variance weighting
ROC-AUC and PR-AUC against the labelled fault windows, plus calibration on the healthy class
anomaly tool; reconstruction attribution per channel feeds explain
Falls back to m14-isolation-forest without torch

limits: Reconstruction error is not a calibrated probability without the healthy-band standardisation
Latent quality is only as good as the healthy reference window

models.title: XAI SHAP Interpretable
models.summary: A SHAP and LIME interpretation wrapper that turns any black-box alert into per-feature attributions a maintenance engineer can argue with. It is the reason a fused score becomes a root cause instead of a number.
entry_points: explain_with_shap(model, X) - dispatches TreeExplainer for tree models, a generic explainer otherwise
Platform adapter also exposes SHAP values on the model output

architecture.detail: TreeExplainer for m10 / m11, a model-agnostic path for everything else
Shapley values with the local-accuracy and missingness properties; contributions sum to the prediction minus the base value
SHAP values + contrastive healthy-band z-scores + feature counterfactuals assembled into the XAI record

io.input: a fitted tree model + feature matrix

advanced.detail: SHAP is not a heuristic: it is the unique additive attribution that satisfies local accuracy, missingness and consistency. That uniqueness is the strongest available defence when an engineer asks why the model blamed a specific channel.
For tree ensembles the Shapley values can be computed in polynomial time, which is why m10 and m11 are the preferred attribution subjects and why the explain tool stays inside a 5 s budget.

A high SHAP value says the channel moved the prediction, not that the channel caused the fault. The platform pairs attributions with contrastive healthy-band deviations and a counterfactual so an operator sees three different kinds of evidence rather than one number dressed up as a cause.
The Hermes narrative is rendered from the adapter's real outputs. If an attribution is unavailable, the explanation says so - the loop is designed to be auditable, not fluent.

layers.detail: The attribution engine of the platform - the explain tool routes here
explain tool: supplies the WHY that operators act on
Description, not evidence - it never contributes to the fused score, only to the justification
Explanations are captured in the DecisionAuditLog with the analysis that produced them

limits: Needs a fitted model to explain - it has no predictive power of its own
Attributions inherit any bias in the underlying model

models.title: XGBoost Tabular Faults
models.summary: Gradient-boosted trees that classify multi-class component states from structured sensor features, and the primary subject of the platform's SHAP explanations. It is the strongest single tabular classifier in the collection and the one most alerts end up resting on.
entry_points: sklearn-API wrapper under the platform adapter (xgboost optional)

architecture.detail: Trees added sequentially, each fitting the second-order Taylor expansion of the loss - the Newton step that made XGBoost fast
Explicit L1/L2 penalties on leaf weights plus a complexity term per tree
One-vs-all softmax over component states

advanced.detail: Boosting with gradient and curvature information converges in far fewer rounds than first-order boosting on the same data. The price is a tighter coupling between loss and implementation - which is why the fallback to m10 exists.

advanced.concept: Regularisation is what prevents memorising the plant
advanced.detail: Leaf-weight penalties and tree complexity terms are the main reason a boosted ensemble does not simply memorise turbine-specific quirks. They are also why the model can be retrained per site without collapsing.

TreeExplainer computes exact Shapley values for this model in polynomial time, so the strongest classifier also produces the most rigorous explanation - the platform's XAI story rests on that pairing.
Its behaviour is what the m25 edge relay approximates with a depth-5 tree, and what m24 compresses to INT8. Accuracy at the centre buys simplicity at the edge.

layers.detail: Primary tabular vote in the fault-classification ensemble
Primary TreeExplainer subject - the explain tool's default
Distilled into the m25 relay and quantized by m24
Receives fallbacks from m01 and m12 when their feature views are unavailable

limits: Tabular only - it cannot see raw waveforms or sequence structure
There are no operator-labelled maintenance records in the collection; the label set comes from the simulator

advanced_layers.name: Fusion engine
advanced_layers.what: Combines the votes of the 25 models into one answer.
advanced_layers.how: Weighted, confidence-weighted, max and median rules; inverse-variance weighting when a model reports uncertainty; coverage-aware probability fusion so a voter that abstains on a class does not dilute it.
advanced_layers.why: Twenty-five opinions are not an answer. Weights come from held-out validation performance in research mode (evaluation.select_weights) and are reported next to any fused score.

advanced_layers.name: Calibrated uncertainty
advanced_layers.what: Every alert carries an interval or a confidence, not just a number.
advanced_layers.how: MC-sampled Bayesian weights (m18), latent-posterior spread (m22), a particle posterior (m16) and the LSTM detector's own interval; expected calibration error is computed at evaluation time.
advanced_layers.why: A number without an interval cannot be compared with another number. Uncertainty is what allows a confident detector to outvote a shaky one, and what makes 'we do not know' a reportable state.

advanced_layers.name: Drift and data trust
advanced_layers.what: Detects that the world, or the sensor, has moved.
advanced_layers.how: Rolling distribution comparison between training and live features (evaluation.drift_report) plus an unsupervised SensorQualityMonitor for freeze, spike, stuck-at and out-of-range conditions.
advanced_layers.why: A detector that fires because the weather changed is worse than no detector. Trust the data before trusting the models - sensor quality flags gate the safety manager and the dashboard's trust badge.

advanced_layers.name: Explainability
advanced_layers.what: Turns an alert into a root cause an engineer can argue with.
advanced_layers.how: m21 SHAP TreeExplainer attributions, contrastive healthy-band z-scores, per-feature counterfactuals, and a Hermes narrative rendered only from real outputs.
advanced_layers.why: Maintenance is a decision made by a person. An explanation that cannot be falsified is not an explanation - attributions are labelled as associations, never as causes.

advanced_layers.name: Physics constraints
advanced_layers.what: Keeps the learning inside what the machine can actually do.
advanced_layers.how: A digital-twin surrogate (m19) supplies residuals and what-if counterfactuals; the PG-BNN (m18) embeds P = tau * omega as a soft penalty and returns physics-consistent uncertainty.
advanced_layers.why: Purely statistical models extrapolate confidently and wrongly outside their envelope. Physics does not replace the detectors - it disagrees with them, visibly.

advanced_layers.name: Safety gate
advanced_layers.what: The one path that is allowed to say STOP.
advanced_layers.how: A depth-5 decision tree exported to model.h for an ESP32 (m25) plus a mirrored in-process SafetyManager evaluating the same hard limits, with hysteresis and cooldown in the alert manager.
advanced_layers.why: Safety is excluded from the ensemble by construction: an average of opinions is not a protection function, and no missing Python dependency may disable a trip.

advanced_layers.name: Evaluation protocol
advanced_layers.what: Makes every number in the collection comparable.
advanced_layers.how: Leak-free window masks, past-only holdout state, ROC-AUC / PR-AUC / calibration / RUL metrics, an experiment tracker, and the fidelity ladder that labels every claim rung 1.
advanced_layers.why: The collection's credibility comes from stating what a metric may claim. Surrogate waveforms, proxy RUL targets and simulator labels are declared on every page rather than buried.

advanced_layers.name: Hermes agent
advanced_layers.what: A Thought -> Action -> Observation loop that decides which model to ask next.
advanced_layers.how: Eight tools: sensor_quality, anomaly, diagnose, explain, rul, safety, what_if, finish. Observations are adapter outputs; the agent never invents a measurement.
advanced_layers.why: Operators do not ask 'what is the SVDD distance'. They ask WHAT, WHERE, WHY, HOW SEVERE, HOW LONG, WHAT NEXT and IS IT SAFE - the loop answers in that order and stops when the question is answered.
